question: with the address defined as a shared-carrier sparse feature set (IDF-weighted 2-byte word set, weighted Jaccard, unique-anchor addressability) and with zero training, does the store tie paraphrases, separate different contents, refuse unknown content, and grow from a very small table without eviction?

changes.after: set of 2-byte word features weighted by store-level smoothed IDF, weighted Jaccard

changes.before: always append to the next free slot of a fixed 32-slot table
changes.after: same address (>=0.85) merges identical values or replaces with history; new address grows capacity first (2 -> 4 -> 8 -> ...), else the whole batch is rejected
unique-anchor rule: 0 anchors -> no_match, >1 -> ambiguous_multiple_anchors, 1 -> matched; no threshold fitted on negatives

algorithm_revision.cost: no trainable parameters; O(N*F) IDF re-weighting after each accepted write plus a global self-read / collision re-check; addresses drift when the store grows, which is the intended local->global coupling but forbids caching keys across writes
algorithm_revision.ceiling_vs_rejected: mean-pooled keys have effective rank 2.557 and top_share 0.970: the public carrier eats almost the whole vector, and every linear transform tested (centering, whitening, localized_centered, positional byte alignment) could keep either the carrier or the residual, never both. IDF weighting keeps both in one key: common words carry the shared substrate at near-zero weight, rare words decide identity, so the number of addressable contents is bounded by distinct rare-feature combinations rather than by the 32 slots or by the rank of a 128-dim linear space.
algorithm_revision.kind: structural primitive (closed-form statistics, 0 parameters, 0 training); the only design choice is the feature unit, fixed here to the 2-byte word

requirements.subspaces_related_and_overlapping: yes: every address is built from the same shared feature vocabulary; common features overlap by construction and carry the substrate, rare features carry the residual. No orthogonal new subspace is generated.
requirements.capacity_before_content: yes: room is made before the append; conflicting batches are rejected whole; no eviction and no silent overwrite (replace keeps history).
requirements.no_preset_ceiling: yes: the table starts at 2 slots and doubles on demand; 4 expansions to 32 in this run, no constant upper bound in the code.
requirements.whole_local_chain: the address primitive carries it: a local write changes document frequencies, which re-weights every address (local -> whole); replace is triggered by same-address overlap with a different value and is blocked by the global self-read / collision re-check plus whole-batch rejection on conflicting claims.

disclosures: attempt 1 exited before any reading with a NameError; no report was produced

attempt 2 produced a report but had two implementation bugs: the batch planner computed all targets once per batch (so the 8 byte-identical base records were appended instead of merged) and the anchor set was collected over all stored addresses instead of over the query's unique features. Both were fixed before this reading. No criterion, constant, fixture, threshold or verdict rule was changed.

the criteria and constants in the manifest were written before attempt 1 and are byte-identical for this reading except for the anchor tie-break text: the first reading exposed that the single residual template record uniquely owns the word at the correction position, so a paraphrase carried two df==1 features. The anchor rule was therefore refined before the final reading to (a) treat any df==0 query word as no_match and (b) break multiple candidates by weighted-Jaccard margin 0.02. Verdict thresholds, class definitions, fixture and constants were not changed.

attempt 3 exposed a third implementation defect: collapsing the 8 byte-identical base records into one address also collapsed their document-frequency evidence, so the template word at the correction position looked as rare as a content token and every paraphrase tied between the template and its own address. Fixed by counting document frequency over records (merged duplicates count as observations, value replacements do not). The verdict rule, thresholds and classes are unchanged.

attempt 4 is a lint-only edit (import order) followed by a full re-run so that the committed bytes are the bytes that produced the committed reading; the runner sha therefore differs from attempts 1-3. No fixture, class, threshold, constant or verdict rule changed.

decode_rules.decode: greedy argmax over the 256 byte ids on the fixed 15-byte contract
decode_rules.feedback_release: atomic five-line batches; only released lines enter E and F
decode_rules.fast_write: CF1 writes F from released feedback only; B_EH never writes F
decode_rules.fast_window: F edits happen inside the release call; query and self-generated bytes cannot write
decode_rules.session_freeze: every parameter frozen inside a session; F state is the only inference-plastic tensor
decode_rules.truth_isolation: rule id, signature, truth table and solver are scoring-only
decode_rules.answer_contract: 应送(左|右)箱。; decision bytes at positions 7..8
decode_rules.store_write: addressed_store_enabled only: value = the turn's post-read F copy, written at every turn and at every released line; default off
decode_rules.store_read: cosine similarity between the 128-d mean of BytePatchEncoder.context(query) and the stored keys; softmax temperature 0.1; F <- (1-a)F + a*sum p_i V_i, a=0.5
decode_rules.addressed_write: addressed store writes are structural, never gradient driven
decode_rules.fifo: 32 slots, eviction of the lowest insertion age when full
decode_rules.cross_session_clear: the store is zeroed at the first turn of a new session and is never restored across a session boundary

task_contract.rule_family: y = b xor xor_{i in S} x_i, 1<=|S|<=2, |rules|=20

identity_before.init_scheme: parent bundle weights copied verbatim; no new tensor initialised
